newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates lower after drop in overnight.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates lower after drop in overnight.

text.p: Interbank rates fell slightly in Monday morning trade due to improvement in market liquidity and after a drop in the overnight rate on Friday, dealers said.

"Rates are softer because market tightness has eased since last week. The overnight was also down last Friday," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "But lenders are not offering much lower as there's still some uncertainty in the market."
One-week money was at 7.40 percent against 7.50 percent on Friday, dealers said.
One- and three-month money were at 7.60/80 percent against 7.70/80 percent.
The overnight rate, which fell to 5.9/6.0 percent on Friday, was expected to trade around 6.0 percent, dealers said.
"Banks were short earlier on the overnight, but they are getting long now," said another dealer.
Market liquidity had improved following maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 1.5 billion ringgit last week.
There will be another maturity of a 500-million ringgit bill issue this week.
Bank Negara has not announced any new issue to roll-over the maturities.

But dealers said an outflow of some two billion ringgit on Thursday due to maturity of funds Bank Negara lent to the market to help ease market tightness last month could prevent rates from falling back to a month ago levels.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were higher across the board, reflecting softening in cash interbank rates.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up four points to 92.56, or an implied yield of 7.44 percent.
The December contract rose five to 92.67, or 7.33 percent and March 1998 was also up five to 92.75, or 7.25 percent.
